candidates.title: The Corner Watch
candidates.one_line_concept: Aachu and Zuv keep saving each other from the same sharp table corner without ever making it a big romantic speech.
candidates.emotional_truth: The most believable care is often a hand quietly appearing between your head and the furniture.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Couples who live in one small room will recognize the automatic palm-on-corner reflex immediately.
candidates.visual_evidence: 3-5 slides: one bends to pick up a charger, the other's hand covers the table corner; later the roles reverse near a shelf; both pretend it is normal; the final frame shows the hand arriving before the bump can happen.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Low, as long as the object stays specific: same table corner, same repeated reflex, mutual care.

candidates.title: The Video Call Cleanup
candidates.one_line_concept: One of them is about to join a call, and the other silently removes the embarrassing life evidence from the camera frame.
candidates.emotional_truth: Love is knowing the difference between private mess and public background.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Anyone who has had a partner whisper-point at laundry, mugs, hair, or an open cupboard before a call will send this.
candidates.visual_evidence: 4-6 slides: laptop camera view open; a towel is visible behind Aachu; Zuv quietly slides it away, straightens one cushion, moves a mug, then gives a tiny off-camera thumbs-up while Aachu keeps a serious meeting face.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium-low; it needs exact background objects and silent teamwork, not a vague work-from-home couple scene.

candidates.title: The Taste-Test Face
candidates.one_line_concept: While cooking, one keeps offering the spoon, and the other's face becomes the actual salt measurement.
candidates.emotional_truth: Some couples do not need recipes; they have one person's dramatic expression and the other person's trust in it.
candidates.relatable_trigger: The send-trigger is the tiny domestic ritual of asking 'is this enough?' without really needing words.
candidates.visual_evidence: 3-5 slides: a pot on the stove, spoon held under Zuv's chin, Aachu watching his face instead of the food; he squints, she adds exactly one pinch; later he offers her the spoon and she makes the same verdict face.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium; cooking couples can become soft-focus filler unless the spoon, pinch, and judging face stay central.

candidates.title: The Kitchen Traffic Jam
candidates.one_line_concept: They keep standing exactly where the other needs to open a drawer, so the whole kitchen becomes a soft, annoyed choreography.
candidates.emotional_truth: Living close together means half your affection is learning how to move around one another badly.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Small-kitchen couples will recognize the hip bump, the half-step aside, and the person who moves but somehow remains in the way.
candidates.visual_evidence: 4-6 slides: Aachu reaches for a drawer blocked by Zuv's leg; he shifts just enough to block the cabinet; she nudges him with her hip; later he needs the spoon drawer and she is the obstacle; final frame shows both laughing in the narrow space.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium-low; must stay mutual and physical, not become 'one partner is useless in the kitchen.'

top_pick.title: The Corner Watch
top_pick.why: It is the cleanest behavior: photographable without caption, mutual, fresh, tactile, emotionally warm, and specific enough to avoid quote-card romance.

rejected_patterns: shared pockets, bags, or item redistribution
scooter, helmet, strap, or road-safety checking
food stealing as the whole idea
one partner as fool and the other as caretaker
risk_notes: Keep every option mutual; the teasing must be affectionate, not a competence joke.
Avoid making the text carry the idea. The behavior has to read from the hand, object, posture, and repeated gesture.
The Corner Watch is strongest because it can become a 3-5 slide escalation without adding plot machinery.
